rites.name: Meranameno
rites.text: Meranameno is a concept of Krouktaggun, held as the sound that ran through the first roots as they condensed out of the Singing. In the Age of the first sovereign, groves took the shape of this concept and kingdoms grew along its lines.

rites.name: Isyuzora
rites.text: Isyuzora is the concept of a resonant bond, a tuned hum that held the first roots of Krouktaggun together before the landfall of the Age of Sundering. It was never a single being but a pattern that surfaced wherever rootstone chose to settle and sing.

rites.name: Vhaikturn
rites.text: Vhaikturn is the concept of a binding oath, the weight a witness gives to a promise made in the Courts of Krouktaggun. It is not a being but a principle that the council of the Courts invokes when a trial must be held to its word. In the Second Era it was the steadying force that kept the doors between worlds from swinging shut on those who had spoken truthfully.

rites.name: Joronulden
rites.text: Joronulden is a concept of Krouktaggun, the principle that a trial is only sealed when the council of the Courts has spoken its name aloud. It was raised during the Holy Age as the old orders bound their temple flames to the doors between worlds.

rites.name: Halerdastar
rites.text: Halerdastar is a concept of Krouktaggun in the Walled Age, a notion that the ordered holding of walls, orders and churches can keep a people whole through centuries of pressure. It is remembered mostly in the stonework of old crossings and the vows sworn at their gates.

rites.name: Silioranae
rites.text: Silioranae is the concept of the wall as a living covenant in Krouktaggun, the belief that a thing held together by oath can outlast the storms that test it. In the Walled Age its orders carried it from village palisade to the great stone rings, and its first crossings were marked by the stones set in gaps where walls had once broken.

rites.name: Thezis
rites.text: Thezis is a concept of the Krouktaggun Walled Age, a doctrine that holds that walls are kept alive by oaths sung at their footings. Orders of wall-wardens taught it through the centuries of holding, and it was tested hardest when landfall broke old bonds during the Age of Sundering.

rites.name: Merataleno
rites.text: Merataleno is a concept in the Krouktaggun cycle, a pattern of seeds that the Library files among the branches of the Three Futures during the Age of the first sovereign. It is less a thing than an idea of how groves and growing kingdoms take root and spread.

rites.name: Seriantanum
rites.text: Seriantanum is a concept in Krouktaggun, the idea that a single act of will can split a future into three shelved branches within the Library of Outcomes. Born during the Age of Sundering, it describes how people who lost their old bonds to landfall learned to rank possible endings and choose one to pursue.
